findings.claim: The saved-note builder decides what counts as code with column-0 rules that ignore list context. As a result it rewrites or removes `[n]` inside fenced code that sits in a list item and is indented 4 or more spaces, and it leaves `[n]` raw in an indented list-continuation paragraph, which it mistakes for an indented code block.
findings.impact: When the viewer saves a thread whose answer has a fenced code block nested under a list item (common in model output, e.g. `1. Step` followed by a fence indented 4 spaces), indexing such as `arr[1]` in that code is silently turned into a `loft://` link or deleted in the note. A loose-list continuation paragraph indented 4 spaces after a blank line keeps raw `[1]` markers that are neither links nor removed. The note differs from what AnswerMarkdown (markdown-it, CommonMark) showed on screen.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/frontend/askNoteFormat.ts rewriteAnswer: the fence opener is detected only by `/^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})/`. A line with 4 or more leading spaces after a non-blank line therefore goes to `rewriteInline`, which runs `rewriteMarkers` on it. The indented-code test `/^(?: {4}|\t)/ && (indented || previousBlank)` treats any 4-space line after a blank as code, including list-item continuation paragraphs. MarkdownPreview uses markdown-it, which parses a fence inside a list item relative to the item's content column. The AskTabThread tests cover only top-level fences, top-level indented code and inline spans.
findings.repro:
Save a thread whose answered turn's answer is "1. Run:
    ```python
    y = arr[1]
    ```" and whose citations are [{n:1, position:{seconds:5}}]. The note line becomes `    y = arr[0:05](loft://<id>?t=5)`, while on screen the fence renders as a code block with `arr[1]`. With no citation for 1 the line becomes `    y = arr`. Second case: "- item

    see [1]" renders as a list paragraph, but the note keeps `[1]` raw.

bucket_proposal.reason: I7 requires that outside code (as 083 step 3 defines it: what AnswerMarkdown renders inside code/pre) every [n] is a loft link or removed, and that inside code the text is as received. Both directions break for list-nested blocks.

findings.proposed_fix: Classify code with the same CommonMark parser AnswerMarkdown uses (markdown-it tokens with `map` line ranges for fence/code_block, and code_inline), and rewrite markers only in text outside those ranges. Add tests for a list-nested fence and a list continuation paragraph.

specification_compliance: 081: trim_history removes markers until none remain, counts sizes after removal, keeps the newest turns while they fit in max_chars//2, and cuts an oversized newest turn question first. The passage budget is max_chars minus the kept sizes, and the ranking text is history[-1].question + "\n" + question (rag.py file_ask_endpoint, file_question.py:159-180, :345-349).

081 I3: FileQuestionTurn has extra=forbid, a question of 1..1000 and an answer of at most 20000, and history max_length=10. Pydantic validation runs before the handler body, so before any gate or slot.

082: the store keeps turns per file, beginAsk empties the text box, settleAsk puts a failed turn's question back only into an empty box, clearAskThread keeps the text, and the history sent is answered turns only, the last 10, with answers sliced to 20000.

084: POST /notes declares only when origin == 'ask_answer', after the commit and the event. A 409 counts as success, other statuses and httpx transport errors answer 502, and trust_declared_at is set only on success. The startup pass reads only ask_answer rows that are still null and runs as a background task. The migration is a plain ADD COLUMN, guarded by an existence check.
I11 (r1): rag.py ends an empty or whitespace-only answer with meta followed by done carrying an error, and sends no citations event.
I12 (r1): /notes, /distill and /note-from-file record and return the path core created, through _created_rel_path.
potential_unspecified_behavior: AskTab recomputes saveContent, including a fresh saved_at timestamp, on every render, because answeredTurns is a new array each time. The note's saved_at is the time of the last render before confirm, not the moment of the click.
The history prompt block writes earlier answers without delimiters. An earlier answer that contains lines such as 'Question:' is inlined verbatim; this is outside the threat model.
regression_risks: POST /notes without an explicit origin defaults to ask_answer (schemas.py:70), so it is declared unverified. In this repository the only caller is AskSaveDialog, which now sends origin explicitly.
The startup pass and the note scanner both start as background tasks at lifespan start. They touch different columns, so I see no conflict, but they run concurrently.
test_coverage: test_spec_addon_081_file_question_history.py covers the limits, marker removal, budget edges (fits exactly and one over), the ranking text, and that no-history and empty-history prompts are equal. It does not compare those prompts against the prompts from before the change.

AskTabThread.test.tsx covers history selection, the button states, failure put-back, the saved-note layout, and code preservation for top-level fences, tilde fences, indented code, inline spans and an unclosed fence. It does not cover list-nested fences or list continuation paragraphs (see R1).
test_spec_addon_084 covers save-route statuses, transport errors, capture notes, the startup pass filtering, retry on the next start, /health not delayed, and migration idempotence and preservation.
The e2e-components ask-thread-desktop case measures the I6 layout against the real AskTab.
not_verified: I did not run any test or build; every behaviour here comes from reading the code.
I did not confirm with a live parser that markdown-it treats a fence indented 4 spaces under '1. ' as a fence. I reasoned it from CommonMark list-item content-column rules.
I did not read InternalClient.declare_trust_tier, so I have not confirmed that every non-2xx answer raises InternalAPIError and every transport failure is an httpx.HTTPError subclass.
I did not check whether the no-history prompt text is byte-identical to the template before this change (I1 against the pre-change state), beyond reading the jinja whitespace control.
The fix-diff record was truncated at 600000 bytes, so I did not see the later fix commits in full.
trajectory: The commits since r1 are mostly develop work merged into the branch: the YouTube frames specs and code (SPEC-ADDON-076..078, SPEC-CORE-058), the reading app (SPEC-CORE-059..063) and YouTube scene tiles (SPEC-ADDON-079..080). For this feature they answered r1's scope findings by giving the YouTube work approved specs on develop, declaring the empty-answer failure and the created-path change as revisions I11 and I12, and renumbering this spec to SPEC-ADDON-081..084. I saw no added branch, state or prediction in the file-Ask-thread design itself. The YouTube storyboard spec, however, was revised three times for tile timing: the sheet duration over the cell count, then 1/fps, then an interval recovered from round(fps*duration). Each round replaced the previous timing rule with a new derived prediction, and min_interval thinning was dropped along the way. That pattern is patching in the YouTube design, not in this change.
